newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqis demonstrate against Turkish incursion.
newsitem.headline: Iraqis demonstrate against Turkish incursion.

text.p: Several hundred demonstrators gathered on Thursday at the Turkish embassy in Baghdad to protest against the Turkish incursion into northern Iraq.
They waved placards and shouted slogans denouncing both Turkey and Israel and demanding that Ankara withdraw its troops immediately from the area.
"Down, down, down Turkey and Israel," screamed several demonstrators and others urged Arab states and Baghdad to force "the covetous murderers" out of Iraqi territory.

Turkey on Wednesday rebuffed calls from Western and Middle Eastern capitals to withdraw its troops immediately from northern Iraq, where they have been fighting separatist Kurdish rebels for the past two weeks.
More than 10,000 Turkish troops streamed into Iraq in pursuit of Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels who use the region as a base to launch raids into southeast Turkey.
Iraq has being condemning the incursion since it started, saying the Turks were coordinating military operations in the area with both Israel and the United States.
The demonstration was the first orchestrated by Iraq against the invasion. The demonstrators submitted a letter of protest to the Turkish charge d'affaires in the embassy.

Taking part were representatives of parties comprising Iraq's progressive national front, including pro-Baghdad Kurdish groups who demanded an immediate pull out and the return of Baghdad authority to the region.
Northern Iraq is outside government control, being under Western air protection since after the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
The Iraqis also held another demonstration against the incursion at the headquarters of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Baghdad.
